COLUMN VALUES FOR FURNITURE: the header band, corner decorations, folio tab, footer rule and foot line are all absolutely positioned page furniture, not flowed content; the allowed column vocabulary here is only full/left/right, so I marked them 'full' - a consumer should honour their measured bbox rather than pour them into a body column. ROLE COMPROMISE: 'Reprint 2026-27' at x=713..870, y=2107..2127 is a page-FOOT running line; there is no running_footer role in the allowed list, so I used running_header - it is the foot line, not a head. Its horizontal centre is x=791.5 px against a page centre of 827 px; I still report align 'center' because the line is conventionally centred and the 35 px offset matches the scan's overall leftward shift (left text margin 107 px vs right 71 px). SPACE_BEFORE CONVENTION: measured as (this element's top - the previous element's bottom) / page height WITHIN THE SAME COLUMN, so the figure rail's gaps are not polluted by the prose column's; the first element of each column is measured from the running header's bottom (y=183), and the top-right decorations get 0.0 because they overlap the header band rather than follow it. FILL/DEPTH: text_block is the measured extent of printed content across both columns (x=107..1425, y=238..1951 px); the folio tab and the foot line sit outside it. page.fill = 0.98 because the left column runs right to the foot of its frame - its last paragraph breaks mid-sentence ('the embryonal axis has the'), so the page is effectively full even though 156 px of white paper remain between the last line (y=1951) and the foot line (y=2107); the right column's content ends higher, at y=1667. SIZE_PT IS DERIVED, SIZE_REL IS MEASURED: dpi is known (200), but converting a measured cap height to a type size needs a font-specific cap ratio, so size_pt values are derived as size_rel x an 11 pt body size, itself inferred from the 14.04 pt leading and the 7.56 pt cap height. Trust size_rel.
